messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — SEV 1: Multiple GPU OOMs observed on stream-decode-prod-*. Auto-pager to #incidents and paging oncall.

incident-bot: Alerts: decode-container OOM (cuda: out of memory) x12 in last 8m across nodes stream-decode-0,1,3. Error sample: `CUDA out of memory while allocating 2.1 GiB`

sara: I'm on it. oncall here. seeing repeat OOMs starting ~02:18 UTC, memory climbs during streaming decode then sudden OOM.

omar: copying logs — seems correlated with single client sending extremely large max_tokens via sticky proxy header. Not normal traffic pattern.

maria-cs: CS reports: a handful of customers hit 5xx drops, customer-zenith reported missing streaming responses around 02:20–02:28 UTC. They reported ~40% of streams failing for a short window.

sara: initial triage: 1) mitigate runaway requests 2) protect nodes 3) restore healthy traffic. Plan to apply a runtime clamp on per-request max_tokens and shift new streams to lower-memory model variant.

sara: Running hotfix: set per-request hard cap to 4096 tokens for streaming routes. Command: ```
# apply clamp to routing/runtime config
rdctl config set --scope route:streaming --key max_tokens_hard_cap --value 4096
rdctl rollout apply --scope route:streaming
```

deploy-bot: Rollout initiated for config route:streaming. 50% canary -> 100% in 90s.

lucas: I started a graceful restart of streaming-decode-pool on k8s to reclaim mem fragmentation: ```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/streaming-decode-pool -n infra
```

infra-oncall: FYI graphs: https://grafana/redwood/decode-memory?panel=streaming-prod — memory spikes at ~02:19 then OOMs. Looking at pmem fragmentation, allocation patterns show long-running KV cache growth for those streams.

omar: Found the client header bug: proxy was concatenating user-provided max_tokens from retries. Some requests ended up with effective max_tokens ~100k. That triggered runaway generation on decode path.

sara: Good catch. Hotfix mitigated new requests. Observed OOM count drop to zero by 02:35 UTC. Old sessions with huge KV cache still occupying memory; restart helped.

maria-cs: Impact summary for CS: ~2 major customer sessions experienced partial loss; estimated 0.8% of overall streaming traffic dropped; peak error rate ~12% for 8m window. Draft message for affected customers ready.

kevin-cs: share draft here, will prepare proactive outreach and offer replay for impacted requests.

maria-cs: Draft: "We experienced a brief service disruption affecting streaming responses due to excessive request sizes from a misconfigured proxy. Root cause identified and mitigations applied. We're offering assistance to reprocess affected requests." :email:

sara: Additional mitigations I'm pushing: 1) add server-side hard reject for requests with tokens > 50k (safety net), 2) add a runtime metric for per-stream KV growth and alert at 75% mem threshold, 3) add GAU for unusual header token sums.

lucas: I'll open infra task to tune eviction for KV cache on streaming runtime. Might help prevent fragmentation causing OOM on long-lived streams.

incident-bot: Change status -> mitigation in progress.

sara: Confirming service stabilized. No new OOMs after clamp and restarts. We'll keep throttling new large streams for 2 hours.

omar: Note to ops: a malformed header caused token inflation. We'll add validation in proxy and a test to simulate header concatenation.

oncall-bot: Handoff: sara -> omar for post-incident monitoring. Leaving notes: applied max_tokens_hard_cap=4096, restarted streaming-decode-pool, routed new streams to streaming-small-1 model for canary. See runbook ID: RB-STREAM-21.

sara: handoff done. @omar please keep eyes for residual elevated latencies or memory creep. I'll join the follow-up postmortem.

omar: Acknowledged. I'll run additional load-cases and validate no regressions. Also will prepare a telemetry alert: trigger when decode OOM > 3 within 10m across pool.

infra-oncall: I've quarantined the affected nodes and marked them as unschedulable until we confirm clean state. Backfill started on healthy nodes.

maria-cs: CS will send customer communications in 20m and offer replays.

sara: TL;DR for incident: root cause = proxy header bug causing runaway max_tokens + missing server-side hard cap. Mitigation = runtime hard cap + restart + routing fallback. Impact = short window of streaming request drops affecting a small set of customers (~0.8% global traffic, peak error rate 12%). Next actions: proxy fix, server-side validation & hard reject, KV eviction tuning, alerting.

sara: Closing pager. Marking incident as resolved -> monitoring. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> monitoring. Postmortem required. Severity: S1. Pager cleared.

kevin-cs: Scheduling post-incident call with CS + Eng tomorrow 16:00 UTC to review customer comms and replay plan.

omar: I'll attach logs, config diffs, and a small repro harness to the postmortem ticket.

sara: Thanks all. Leaving oncall notes in the ticket.

oncall-bot: oncall handoff complete.
